content: Constancy in love is an eternal inconstancy, which causes our heart to attach itself successively to all the qualities of the person we love.
author: François de La Rochefoucauld
story:
A high French aristocrat and military officer wounded in the civil wars of the Fronde, La Rochefoucauld retired from treacherous court intrigue into the brilliant Parisian literary salons of Madame de Sablé. Sharpening his observations into ruthless epigrams, he dissected the flattering illusions of human morality, exposing how self-love (amour-propre) and vanity subtly disguise our most celebrated virtues.

This timeless reminder speaks to the universal struggle to balance inner truth with outer demands. François de La Rochefoucauld understood that the measure of a meaningful life is not external approval, but the quiet integrity with which we meet each day's encounters.
